wu: Yesterday Timeline: Students draw a simple timeline on paper. Teacher asks 'What did you do yesterday?' and students write 2-3 activities with pictures. Volunteers share their timeline with a partner using 'Yesterday I...'
wuAlt: Find Someone Who... Past: Students walk around asking 'Did you...?' questions (e.g., 'Did you watch TV?') and write names. Teacher reviews answers as a class.
Flashcard Recall: Teacher shows 5 flashcards of daily activities (e.g., cook, walk, clean). Students say the past form and make a sentence: 'Yesterday I...'.
pres: Christmas Culture Story: Teacher shows a photo of a Christmas tree. Reads a short story: 'Last week, I decorated my home. I bought a tree. I hung lights. I baked cookies.' Underlines all -ed verbs. Checks understanding: 'What did I do?' and 'When did I do it?'
presAlt: Realia Demonstration: Teacher brings a small decorated box. 'Yesterday, I opened the box. I found a gift. I smiled.' Students repeat and ask questions.
Video Clip: Plays a 1-minute clip of someone preparing for a local holiday (e.g., Eid). Pauses to ask 'What did he/she do?' and elicit past tense sentences.
prac: -ed Pronunciation Sort: Students receive 15 verb cards (e.g., walked, played, watched). In pairs, they sort them into three columns: /t/ (liked), /d/ (opened), /ɪd/ (wanted). Teacher models and monitors pronunciation.
pracAlt: Past Simple Bingo: Teacher calls out base verbs (e.g., 'walk'). Students cross off the past form (walked) on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Chain Drill: Teacher starts a story: 'Yesterday, I woke up.' Student 1 adds: 'I brushed my teeth.' Student 2 adds: 'I ate breakfast.' Continue around the class.
ls: Christmas Culture Listening: Students listen to a 1-minute audio about how Christmas is celebrated in Morocco. They listen and tick activities mentioned (e.g., 'exchange gifts', 'eat special food'). Teacher plays audio twice and reviews answers.
re: Past Tense Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher shows a flashcard (e.g., 'clean'). First student runs to the board, writes 'cleaned', runs back. Next student does the same with a new verb. Team with most correct wins.
prod: Holiday Memory Roleplay: In pairs, Student A is a tourist asking 'What did you do last Eid?'. Student B answers using 3-4 past verbs. Swap roles. Teacher provides sentence frames: 'Last Eid, I...', 'I... with my family.'
rw: Seasonal Text Reading: Students read a short text about 'A Good Day in Oujda'. Underline all -ed verbs. Then write 3 sentences about their own good day using those verbs (e.g., 'I walked in the park. I talked to my friend. I smiled a lot.')
st: Song + Goodbye: Play 'Jingle Bells' with lyrics adapted to past tense ('Yesterday I decorated a tree...'). End with recap: 'Today we talked about past events. Thank you, class. Have a good day!'
g: Student draws a past verb (e.g., 'cooked') and others guess 'Did you cook?'
Teacher says a base verb; teams race to write the past form on the board.
Students scan the seasonal text and circle all -ed verbs within 2 minutes.
Students sit in a circle. Each adds a past verb to a growing story (e.g., 'I walked... and I talked...').
Students match base verbs to their past forms in a speed-matching activity.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 5-sentence story about a bad day using past verbs.
Support: Use a word bank with 10 past verbs to complete sentences.
hw: Write 6 sentences about a good day you had last week.
Interview a family member about their day yesterday and write 3 sentences.
Draw 4 pictures of things you did yesterday and label them in past tense.
tip: For adults, connect past tense to personal stories (e.g., 'Last week, I visited the American Space'). This builds confidence and respects their life experience.
